conventions.convention: Quotients are sheafifications on the big fppf site; G/H uses right translation. Rational orbit sets are distinct from quotient-sheaf sections.
Stabilizers are scheme-theoretic and tested over every k-algebra, including nonreduced algebras. Reduced-orbit factorization is not automatic for nonsmooth groups.
P(V) parametrizes invertible quotients; the space of lines in V is P(V dual). Its action sends L to r(g)L.
The orbit-dimension and smaller-boundary-orbit theorem assumes an algebraically closed field and a connected smooth finite-type group.
Surfaces are integral, smooth over the arbitrary ground field, and projective of pure dimension two. O(K_X)=ω_X=exterior-square Ω¹; χ is computed over that ground field, without assuming H⁰(O_X)=k.
Numerical equivalence tests intersection against every invertible sheaf. N¹_R is the real scalar extension of Pic modulo numerical triviality; its definition does not assume finite dimension.
The general Hodge theorem requires H²>0, not ampleness. Equality means numerical triviality; the finite-dimensional signature conclusion is conditional on finite Picard number.
Ideal order is maximal-ideal-adic order, not Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity; the zero ideal has order +∞ and the unit ideal has order zero.
Resolution boundaries have a fixed total order, disjoint components within each member, and no component repeated between members.
A controlled transform divides by the exceptional ideal to the marking power. An extension inserts only isomorphisms and retains every original nontrivial blowup.
Support-clearing canonical resolution requires positive marking and generic nonvanishing on every smooth component; marking zero is not covered.
The core canonical-resolution proposition is over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field under AC; descent extends the final construction to arbitrary characteristic-zero fields.
Ordinary-derivative support converses require characteristic zero or a perfect field of characteristic p with marking μ<p. The forward support inclusion holds in every characteristic.
Restriction to a boundary stratum omits boundary members containing that component; the remaining restricted boundary must satisfy the SNC convention.
Step 1a counts the strict transforms of the boundary fixed when Step 1 begins; newly created exceptional divisors remain in the full boundary but do not enter that count.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, a marked ideal with μ≥1 on a smooth finite-type scheme, generically nonzero on every irreducible component, admits a canonical resolution with upper-semicontinuous invariants, regular SNC maximal centers, strict descent of (inv,ν) above centers, unchanged invariants off centers, and étale compatibility up to insertion of isomorphisms.

Under AC and characteristic zero, two tangent directions of a maximal-order marked ideal at a support point, both transversal to E, admit common étale neighbourhoods identifying their homogenized marked ideals and tangent equations, agreeing on support, and identifying the induced homogenized transforms and maximal-contact strict transforms along every multiple test blowup.

Under AC, μ≥1 and characteristic zero or perfect characteristic p>μ, for a maximal-order marked ideal and regular S in SNC position with E not contained in its support, supp(I,μ)∩S=supp(C(I,μ)|S). The equality persists along centers contained in or disjoint from the strict transforms of S; every restricted test sequence lifts to an ambient one with centers in those strict transforms.

Under AC, every positive-marked ideal generically nonzero on every component of a smooth finite-type scheme over an arbitrary characteristic-zero field has a canonical resolution obtained by descent of the algebraic-closure resolution; it commutes with smooth morphisms, has the mark-one empty-boundary ambient-embedding comparison, and is natural under ground-field isomorphisms.

Under AC, a reduced closed subscheme Y of a smooth finite-type scheme over a characteristic-zero field has a canonical embedded desingularization by regular SNC centers avoiding the original smooth locus of Y; its strict transform is smooth and SNC with the exceptional divisor, and the construction commutes with smooth morphisms and smooth ambient embeddings.

Under AC, for a smooth finite-type group over any field acting on a separated finite-type scheme and x∈X(k), the orbit subscheme is locally closed, G-stable, smooth and finite type, and G→O_x is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation.

For any finite-type k-group acting on separated finite-type X and x∈X(k), G_x is a closed subgroup scheme; a nonempty rational-point fibre is an fppf right G_x-torsor trivialized by a finite field extension, rational translates are g₀G_x, and (g,h)↦(g,gh) identifies G×G_x with G×_XG, also with the kernel pair over a factored locally closed orbit.

Under AC, over any field, the fppf quotient G/H of a smooth affine finite-type group by any closed subgroup scheme is a separated finite-type scheme, with faithfully flat locally finitely presented projection; a representation and scheme-theoretic line stabilizer realize it as a locally closed orbit in P(V dual). No smoothness of H is required.

Under AC, for every invertible L on an integral smooth projective surface over any field, χ(X,L)=χ(X,O_X)+(L²−L·K_X)/2; equivalently χ(O_X(D))=χ(O_X)+D·(D−K_X)/2 for every Cartier divisor D. No effectivity, ampleness or vanishing hypothesis is imposed.

Under AC, an ample H on an integral smooth projective surface over any field meets every nonzero effective Cartier divisor positively and has H²>0. An invertible sheaf with a nonzero section has nonnegative intersection with H, with equality only when that section is nowhere vanishing and the sheaf is trivial.
Under AC, on an integral smooth projective surface over any field, H²>0 and L·H=0 imply L²≤0, with equality if and only if L is numerically trivial. H need not be ample.

Under AC, every integral separated finite-type scheme over a characteristic-zero field has a canonical smooth proper birational resolution, isomorphic over its smooth locus, compatible with smooth base change and equivariant under every scheme-automorphism group action, including actions not preserving the ground field.

concerns.concern: Statement line 33 adds: “In particular the resolution is controlled by the induced multiple test blow-up of the restricted marked ideal on the regular hypersurface V(u).” The hypotheses require only a tangent direction, not SNC/transversality with E. For X=A², I=(x,y)², μ=2, E={V(x),V(y)}, and u=x+y, all stated hypotheses hold, but both boundary members restrict to the same origin divisor on V(u). This violates def-simple-normal-crossings-divisors' prohibition on repeated components, so the advertised restricted marked ideal/test sequence is not defined under the current boundary convention. The support-containment assertion itself survives this example.

Proof 2.2, line 106, chooses tangent directions after Step 1a and invokes F4 for restriction and F3 for gluing, without establishing SNC with the full current boundary or transversality of both directions. The inherited boundary missing the support does not remove newly created exceptional divisors from E_i. lem-coefficient-ideal-restriction-support and lem-glueing-homogenized-ideals require those hypotheses. The complete source argument, Włodarczyk https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0401401, §3 Step 1bb, printed pp.18–19, instead chooses directions on the earlier input and transports their hypersurfaces and comparison neighbourhoods through the preceding test sequence. The current proof needs that transport argument or an explicit proof that its newly chosen directions satisfy the cited hypotheses.

alerts.finding: F5, line 63, states for a smooth group over an unspecified field that “the orbit of a k-point of minimal dimension among the orbits in a G-stable closed subset is closed”, citing lem-orbit-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-dimension. That supplier assumes an algebraically closed field and a connected group. Over R, the smooth connected anisotropic torus a²+b²=1 acts on P¹ by matrices [[a,−b],[b,a]]. Every real-point orbit has dimension one and hence minimal rational-orbit dimension, but its scheme orbit is P¹ minus the conjugate eigenlines [1:±i], so it is not closed. Proof 1.1 correctly passes to an algebraic closure before F5 is used; this finding concerns the overbroad fact and citation, not a counterexample to the Borel fixed-point theorem.
